ONE-TIME SETUP

Your world. A second screen.

  1. Install the companion addon

    Extract AzerothLiveMap into your Anniversary Interface/AddOns folder. Restart WoW and enable it in the AddOns list.

    ↓ Download addon (.zip)
  2. Place your data block

    Use /alm size 2 for a 100 × 80 block with fast quest sync. Type /alm unlock, drag its handle, then /alm lock. Keep all five rows visible. /alm sync compact uses one smaller row with slower quest sync.

  3. Connect your game

    Choose Connect WoW here, then share the WoW window or its monitor. Move this app to your other monitor. A new session needs a fresh sharing choice.

If the tiny strip is hard to read, try /alm size 3 or /alm size 4. Use /alm show if hidden or /alm reset to return it to the top-left. Minimized, hidden, or frozen capture sources cannot provide live updates.

Built for Anniversary 2.5.6. Enable Questie alongside companion addon 0.4.0 for quest pickups, objectives, and turn-ins across all Questie-generated zones. Browse a zone to see its received pins. Fast mode sends four quest packets at once; overall progress and packet rate appear in the sidebar. Initial sync depends on total quest data and capture quality. Questie’s character and map filters apply. Live-client verification is still required.
YOUR MAP, ITS OWN WINDOW

A companion for your second screen.

Launch Azeroth Live Map from your Linux application menu after installing the project’s companion launcher. It opens this map in a dedicated window.

Or, in Chrome or Chromium, open the browser menu and choose Install Azeroth Live Map if available. Installation options vary by browser.

Move the window to your second monitor, choose Connect WoW, and select your game. Your map preferences are remembered; screen sharing starts only when you choose it.

The app shell can reopen offline after its first successful load. Map artwork still needs an internet connection. Live tracking needs WoW and an active screen share.
